scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You tick a box that says I'm not a robot, and somehow it believes you. How can one click prove you're human?

scenes.name: name
scenes.text: CAPTCHA is a test that computers give, to tell humans and bots apart. Bots are used to spam, scalp tickets and break into accounts.

scenes.name: old
scenes.text: Older captchas showed warped letters or blurry images, things that were easy for people but hard for computers.

scenes.name: behaviour
scenes.text: Modern ones quietly watch how you behave. How your mouse moves, how you scroll and type, and details about your browser.

scenes.name: score
scenes.text: All of that becomes a risk score. Look normal, and one click is enough, or no test at all.

scenes.name: puzzle
scenes.text: Look suspicious, maybe using a VPN or private browsing, and you get the traffic lights and crosswalks puzzle.

scenes.name: ai
scenes.text: AI can now solve many image puzzles, so captchas rely more and more on behaviour, and keep changing.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Watch, score, challenge, adapt. Proving you're human. Follow for more on how things really work.
